thesis: Organize every city around the traveller decision it resolves, not around a catalogue of attractions. The agent asks only the smallest set of questions that can change the city, route, pace or safety boundary.

release_policy.publishable_label: research-based draft; human review required for dated delivery
escalation_triggers: religious, craft, farm or teacher access

product_units.label: Shanghai

identity.what_it_is: A readable city-scale contrast between river, historic fabric, migration and contemporary urban life.
identity.not_for: A tower-and-shopping checklist or an unverified Tai Chi/creative-studio promise.

include_when: architecture or urban history is a priority
the traveller wants a gentle first China city
the traveller needs a strong public-transport base
protect: one coherent neighbourhood question per half day
arrival and recovery time
exclude_or_split_when: one-night stop with no full day
the request depends on private homes, teachers or studios without a current partner record

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Do you want to photograph façades, understand their history, or see how old buildings are reused today?
latent_need_rules.effect: Chooses the reading layer and prevents an overfilled landmark loop.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: What time can you actually leave your hotel on the first full day, and are mobile data and payment already working?
latent_need_rules.effect: Protects the first day from a false full-day assumption.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Would one more Shanghai neighbourhood be better than adding Hangzhou or Suzhou with another transfer?
latent_need_rules.effect: Decides whether to keep Shanghai deep or extend to Jiangnan.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Would a public, consent-based observation route still meet your aim if a private introduction is unavailable?
latent_need_rules.effect: Converts private-access expectations into a safe public alternative.

follow_up_questions.ask: How many protected full days do you have after arrival and before departure?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Sets the route depth and whether a Jiangnan extension is realistic.

follow_up_questions.ask: Do you want façades and photographs, historical context, or contemporary urban reuse?
Any mobility needs, children, older relatives, or limits on stairs and long walks?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Changes the walking loop, seating and transfer plan.

follow_up_questions.ask: Do you have an extra night for Jiangnan, or would another Shanghai day be more valuable?
Is your priority observation, a beginner session, or serious training—and what English instruction and physical limits matter?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Routes to human review before any teacher is mentioned.

human_review_triggers: mobility, medical, severe allergy or child-safety constraints
output_emphasis: explain one urban relationship
give a calm main route and a rain/low-energy branch
name what to delete rather than add

product_units.label: Hangzhou–Suzhou

identity.what_it_is: A Jiangnan choice: lake/tea/temple rhythm or gardens/canals/craft, with transfer cost made explicit.
identity.not_for: Shanghai plus two water-town day trips squeezed into one day.

include_when: the traveller has at least three protected nights
landscape, tea, gardens or canals are the actual question
a slower regional contrast is more valuable than another megacity
protect: choose Hangzhou or Suzhou as the primary question before combining them
one overnight when the traveller wants depth
exclude_or_split_when: same-day return is mandatory and the traveller wants both cities
the trip has less than three protected nights

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Must this be a same-day return from Shanghai, or can you protect one overnight?
latent_need_rules.effect: Determines whether a coherent route is possible.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Would you rather read lake/tea/temple landscapes or gardens/canals/craft in detail?
latent_need_rules.effect: Chooses one Jiangnan identity instead of stacking similar scenery.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: What weather, walking or stair threshold requires a shorter or indoor alternative?
Are you learning about the material culture, buying something, or seeking a verified participatory activity?

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you willing to stay overnight, or must this be a same-day return from Shanghai?
Do you want lake/tea/temple pace or gardens/canals/craft density—and how many days can you truly protect?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Chooses Hangzhou versus Suzhou and the night split.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you mainly learning, buying, watching a current programme, or seeking a verified hands-on activity?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Sets the research-only or human-check boundary.

follow_up_questions.ask: What terrain and weather can your group comfortably handle?
Which city comes before and after Jiangnan, and where is your recovery buffer?

output_emphasis: state the one Jiangnan question
show transfer time as part of the product
offer one city first and the other as a deliberate extension

product_units.label: Beijing

identity.what_it_is: A first-China historical grammar: imperial scale, civic ritual, neighbourhood life and one deliberate Great Wall choice.
identity.not_for: Every palace, park, hutong and Wall section in a short stay.

include_when: first visit and history/architecture matter
the traveller can protect three full nights
the Great Wall is treated as a separate logistics decision
protect: one imperial site deeply
a full Wall day only when transport, weather and body cost fit
exclude_or_split_when: less than three nights with both Palace Museum and Wall as musts
mobility or heat limits are unknown for a long exposed day

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: For the Wall, what matters most: iconic first visit, mountain scenery, fewer crowds, or minimising transfers?
latent_need_rules.effect: Chooses the Wall branch instead of a generic recommendation.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Do you want one major imperial site done deeply, or a comparison across two different sites?
How comfortable are you with stairs, uneven ground and a long day outside the city?
latent_need_rules.effect: Sets the physical route and stop rule.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Would you rather see a lively famous lane or a quieter street with less to “do”?

follow_up_questions.ask: What date and time do you land, and do you already have your first full day free?
Is the Great Wall an absolute priority, and are you choosing iconic access, scenery, fewer crowds or minimal transfer?
Do you prefer one imperial site deeply or a comparison across two sites?
Do you want lively famous lanes or quieter neighbourhood fabric?
What are the walking, stair, meal and rest limits for your group?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Changes route length and Wall feasibility.

human_review_triggers: identity-linked reservations and current opening hours
output_emphasis: teach one spatial/history idea
make the Wall an explicit yes/no decision
protect a recovery half-day

product_units.label: Chengdu–Chongqing

identity.what_it_is: A contrast pair: Chengdu protects pace, food and public life; Chongqing creates vertical movement, river-port history and night intensity.
identity.not_for: A checklist that gives each city one rushed night.

include_when: the traveller has at least four protected nights
they want two genuinely different urban rhythms
a high-speed rail transfer is acceptable
protect: at least two nights per city for a first visit
one full transfer/recovery buffer when arrival times are awkward
exclude_or_split_when: less than four nights
the traveller wants slow time but also many remote day trips
Dazu/Wulong is being treated as a casual Chongqing add-on

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Do you want a slower public-life and food rhythm, a vertical high-intensity city experience, or both?
Are pandas a must, and are you open to an early start or longer transfer for them?
latent_need_rules.effect: Prevents pandas from consuming Chengdu by default.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: How many protected nights can each city receive after the train transfer?
What walking, stair, late-night and rest limits should control the Chongqing route?

follow_up_questions.ask: How many protected nights can you give each city after the high-speed rail transfer?
Would you rather protect Chengdu’s slower food/public-life rhythm or Chongqing’s vertical/night intensity?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Clarifies what the two cities must each do.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are pandas a must, or would a city-based Chengdu day be more valuable?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Controls early start and remote transfer.

follow_up_questions.ask: How long can your group walk, climb stairs and stay out after dark?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Changes Chongqing route and night photography.

follow_up_questions.ask: Is the priority a city experience or a separate full-day heritage/landscape excursion?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Prevents remote excursions being hidden add-ons.

human_review_triggers: stairs, heat, family or late-night constraints
output_emphasis: state what each city answers
recommend deleting one city when nights are insufficient
treat cyberpunk as a physical city experiment, not a slogan

product_units.label: Guangzhou–Shenzhen

identity.what_it_is: South China through Cantonese food/trade history and Shenzhen’s public-facing technology and urban systems.
identity.not_for: A promised factory, private company, supplier or R&D visit.

include_when: the traveller wants food/trade plus technology/design
there are at least four protected nights
public observation is acceptable
protect: one food/social question in Guangzhou
one public technology question in Shenzhen
exclude_or_split_when: the request depends on private company access
less than four nights and both cities are treated as equal musts
a border crossing is assumed without current official confirmation

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Is the trip primarily about Cantonese food/trade, public technology, or the contrast between them?
Are you seeking public learning and observation, or private company/supplier access?
Are you buying a personal item, sourcing commercially, or understanding the supply-chain ecosystem?
latent_need_rules.effect: Prevents shopping folklore and legal/IP overreach.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: What transfer, heat and luggage constraints apply to your final day?
latent_need_rules.effect: Changes route order and border decisions.

follow_up_questions.ask: Is your main question Cantonese food/trade, Shenzhen technology, or the contrast between them?
Are you seeking public observation or private company/supplier access?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Determines whether the request can be handled.

follow_up_questions.ask: What food format and dietary limits should the route respect?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Controls meal selection and safety review.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you observing, buying a personal item, sourcing, or photographing the ecosystem?
What passport/visa status and official current basis apply to any border crossing?

human_review_triggers: public access, photography and IP at markets
border, payment, weather and departure logistics
output_emphasis: make public/private access explicit
explain Guangzhou and Shenzhen as different questions
never use company-name tourism as a promise

product_units.label: Guilin–Yangshuo

identity.what_it_is: A weather-aware karst landscape route where river, land, settlement and rest are chosen deliberately.
identity.not_for: A scenic checklist that assumes perfect visibility, cycling ability or water conditions.

include_when: the traveller has three protected nights
landscape is the central question
they accept weather and water-dependent alternatives
protect: one primary landscape mode
a weather fallback and a non-riding option
exclude_or_split_when: Longji is added without a separate full day
the traveller needs guaranteed sunrise/fog/water conditions
cycling/boat safety limits are unknown

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Is the priority river, walking/cycling, photography, family slow travel, adventure or rest?
Will you walk, cycle, use an e-bike, use vehicle support, or avoid road riding?
What weather, water, stairs or walking threshold requires a route change?
latent_need_rules.effect: Ensures the route can survive poor conditions.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Do you have a separate full day for Longji, or should the karst route remain focused?

follow_up_questions.ask: What is the main landscape experience: river, walking/cycling, photography, family slow travel, adventure or rest?
Are you comfortable with a long boat day, motion, weather uncertainty and luggage handling?
Will you ride, walk, use vehicle support, or avoid road riding altogether?
Do you have a separate full day and weather/terrain tolerance for rice terraces?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Makes Longji an explicit add-on decision.

follow_up_questions.ask: What conditions would make you switch to a seated or lower-exposure landscape day?

human_review_triggers: weather, water level, visibility and outdoor access
cycling, e-bike, boat or terrain safety
output_emphasis: describe a landscape relationship, not a view-point list
show the fallback before the guest needs it
never guarantee weather or visibility

product_units.label: Quanzhou–Dehua

identity.what_it_is: A world-port system of trade, religious exchange, everyday streets and a separate ceramics extension.
identity.not_for: A temple checklist, guaranteed private religious access or a ceramic workshop promise.

include_when: the traveller wants maritime history, religious plurality, food or ceramics
there are three protected nights for city plus optional Dehua
the traveller accepts etiquette and consent boundaries
protect: two city days before considering Dehua
one coherent maritime/faith question rather than many temples
exclude_or_split_when: only two days and Dehua is a must
the request requires private homes, religious ritual or maker access
weather/transfer conditions are not current

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Do you want to understand trade systems, port infrastructure, religious exchange, ceramics, or the links between them?
Are you looking for historical context, sacred architecture or living practice—and are you comfortable with strict etiquette and access limits?
Do you have a separate third day for Dehua, or should the city route stay focused on Quanzhou?
Are you learning production context, buying ceramics, or seeking a verified making encounter?

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you most interested in trade systems, religious exchange, everyday city life, ceramics, or the connections between them?
Do you want historical context, sacred architecture or living practice—and what etiquette/access limits are you comfortable with?
Do you have a separate day for Dehua, or would another Quanzhou day be more valuable?
Are you learning, buying, or seeking a verified participatory craft encounter?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Routes to research-only or human review.

follow_up_questions.ask: What weather, walking, stairs or transfer threshold requires a shorter alternative?

human_review_triggers: any private home, ritual or community request
output_emphasis: use the maritime system as the organizing frame
make Quanzhou versus Dehua a real choice
respect living religious and craft communities

product_units.label: Jingdezhen

identity.what_it_is: A living porcelain system: material, kiln, labour, standards, trade and contemporary making.
identity.not_for: An art-market guarantee, private studio access, authentication or shipping service.

include_when: ceramics, material culture, design or craft is a real priority
the traveller has at least two nights
the visitor can distinguish public learning from professional training
protect: one process/history question and one contemporary making layer
delivery and firing uncertainty when a workshop is considered
exclude_or_split_when: the request is only “buy the best porcelain”
a private studio, residency or apprenticeship is assumed
departure is too soon for firing/delivery

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Are you interested in material/process, history, contemporary art, buying, a short workshop, or professional learning?
Do you want a one-off public experience or genuine skills learning, and when do you depart relative to firing or delivery?
Are you exploring a professional programme rather than tourism? If so, what duration, language and portfolio constraints apply?
latent_need_rules.effect: Escalates to a separate research scope.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Are you browsing or buying for personal use? The roadbook cannot authenticate, value or ship objects.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you here for material/process, imperial history, contemporary art, buying, a short workshop, or professional learning?
Do you want a one-off public experience or genuine skills learning, and when do you depart?
Are you browsing, buying for personal use, collecting, or arranging delivery?
Is this professional research or tourism, and how much time can you actually spend?
follow_up_questions.decision_effect: Routes out of the travel product.

follow_up_questions.ask: Would you rather deepen Jingdezhen’s porcelain system or add a separate Fujian production chapter?

human_review_triggers: purchase, provenance, pricing, firing or shipping questions
output_emphasis: teach the production system
separate public observation from private making
never imply authenticity or investment advice

product_units.label: Wudang Mountains

identity.what_it_is: Mountain-based Taoist architectural heritage approached through public space, weather, body cost and etiquette.
identity.not_for: A mystical, healing, master-access or guaranteed Tai Chi training product.

include_when: heritage architecture, Taoist history or mountain walking is the actual question
the traveller can protect three nights and a weather buffer
public heritage routes are acceptable
protect: arrival/departure buffer
stairs, cable-car and weather decision before naming a route
exclude_or_split_when: the traveller wants a guaranteed master, ritual or healing outcome
a day trip leaves no usable mountain day
fitness/medical constraints are undisclosed

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Are you here for public heritage/architecture, mountain walking, a beginner session, or serious training?
latent_need_rules.effect: Separates a travel route from training/health claims.

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Where do you arrive from, how many complete mountain days remain, and can one day move for weather?
Would a respectful public heritage route meet your aim if private religious access is unavailable?
What mobility, stair, altitude, injury or child-safety limits need human review?

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you primarily here for public heritage/architecture, mountain walking, an introductory Tai Chi session, or serious training?
Where do you arrive from, how many actual nights are protected, and can one day change for weather?
Are there stairs, altitude, injury, heart, or child-safety limits that require human review?
Would a respectful public heritage route meet your interest? Private religious access and ritual participation cannot be promised.
Can you accept a weather-dependent fallback and verify same-day operating information?

human_review_triggers: stairs, cable car, weather and mountain transport
Tai Chi, martial arts, healing or training requests
private religious access or ritual participation
medical, injury, family or safety constraints
output_emphasis: lead with architecture and public heritage
show body cost and weather reversibility
refuse mystical or healing claims clearly

product_units.label: Jingmai Mountain

identity.what_it_is: A living tea-forest cultural landscape of villages, roads, ecology and slow observation.
identity.not_for: Tea authentication, investment, health claims, private farmer visits or guaranteed mist/sunrise.

include_when: the traveller has three or more mountain nights
they accept road/weather variability and community etiquette
learning is more important than buying or private access
protect: arrival/departure and road buffer
an approved public/consented observation route
exclude_or_split_when: two nights leave no complete mountain day
the trip depends on private homes or ceremonies
the traveller expects guaranteed tea quality, weather or transport

latent_need_rules.confirmation_question: Are you trying to understand tea landscape and processing, taste comparatively, buy for personal use, or collect?
Would a respectful public or approved observation meet your aim if private homes, gardens or ceremonies are unavailable?
Where do you arrive and leave, and can you accept a weather-dependent road and trail fallback?
Are you seeking medical advice or an investment recommendation? Neither can be supplied through a travel roadbook.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you learning about tea landscape and processing, tasting comparatively, buying for personal use, or collecting?
Would a respectful public/approved observation meet your aim? Private homes, tea gardens and ceremonies cannot be promised.
Where do you arrive from and leave for, and how many complete mountain days remain after transfers?
What walking, mud, stairs, child-safety, injury or health constraints need human review?
Can you accept a weather-dependent fallback and independently verify same-day road/trail conditions?

human_review_triggers: roads, weather, trails and local transport
private farmer, home, ceremony or village requests
output_emphasis: treat tea as landscape and labour, not a product catalogue
put logistics before romantic language
use research-only status until local consent and road checks exist
